dish: Korean fried chicken (original crispy / soy / honey butter), jjajangmyeon, army stew
address: Punggol Coast Hawker Centre, Punggol, Singapore (stall no. + postal to confirm at geocode)
w: A Korean-owned hawker stall in the new Punggol Coast centre frying shatter-crisp Korean chicken by the half or whole (original, sweet-spicy, soy, honey butter), plus jjajangmyeon and army stew — picked by Women's Weekly and Honeycombers among the centre's stalls actually worth eating.

dish: Signature superior seafood soup (prawns, fish maw, pork slices) with hor fun or you mian, fried fish sticks
w: A homegrown soup specialist since 2011: a sweet-savoury, light seafood broth loaded with prawns, fish maw, pork slices, abalone slices and beancurd-skin fish sticks, over rice, hor fun or you mian — with an addictive chilli and fresh lard. Featured by Eatbook (Punggol guide) and reviewed by Seth Lui.

dish: Australian-style brunch — big brekkie, fluffy pancakes, mushroom chicken chop
w: Punggol's go-to waterfront brunch cafe: Australian-inspired big brekkies, avo toast, soft fluffy pancakes and generous mains like the mushroom chicken chop — picked by Eatbook's Punggol guide and City Nomads' Sengkang–Punggol dining guide.

dish: Fuzhou oyster cake with two whole oysters, minced meat and shrimp; kimchi oyster cake
n: Sixth Floor Oyster Cake (Northshore Plaza) — CLOSED
address: Northshore Plaza I, 407 Northshore Drive #02-41, Singapore
w: A Punggol home business (named for the owner's sixth-floor HDB flat) that grew into a Northshore Plaza kiosk frying ultra-crisp Fuzhou oyster cakes — two whole oysters, minced meat and shrimp — covered by Eatbook and Women's Weekly. CLOSED: both outlets shut permanently after 28 Sep 2025 (Seth Lui).

dish: Nasi rendang, lontong kampung, mee rebus, Malay kueh
address: One Punggol Hawker Centre, 1 Punggol Drive #02-08, Singapore 828629
w: Third-generation hawker Madam Fauziah Isnin stirs a secret 15-spice beef rendang in 15–20 kg batches, served as nasi rendang or with lontong kampung, alongside mee rebus, mee soto and Malay kueh — a family recipe line going back to her grandparents' 1940s pop-up. Picked by Women's Weekly and Seth Lui at One Punggol.

dish: Curry puffs — original, sardine, black-pepper chicken, char siew chicken, cheese
address: Punggol Coast Hawker Centre #02-K76, Punggol, Singapore
w: Three young hawkerpreneurs (the Lim brothers and cook Oh Chin Jie) reinventing the curry puff — char siew chicken, cheese-pull and sardine puffs alongside the original — from a Changi Village start in Dec 2024; the July 2025 Punggol Coast stall became their strongest outlet, with puffs typically sold out by 2.30pm (Vulcan Post). Also named by Eatbook and Time Out.

dish: Teochew-style steamed whole fish (grouper, seabass, pomfret) with preserved vegetables, tomato and tofu
n: Hee Hee Hee Steamed Fish & Seafood (Punggol Coast)
address: Punggol Coast Hawker Centre, 84 Punggol Way, Singapore 829911 (stall no. to confirm)
w: Two young fishmongers' steamed-fish stall: the day's catch steamed Teochew-style with preserved vegetables, tomatoes and tofu in a light, tangy broth, or Cantonese-style with scallion and ginger — a whole grouper from about $10. Picked by Honeycombers (12 must-tries) and Women's Weekly at Punggol Coast.

dish: Prata and banana-leaf rice with mutton curry
n: SJ Sickander Ammal Muslim Food (Punggol Coast)
address: Punggol Coast Hawker Centre, 84 Punggol Way, Singapore 829911 (stall no. to confirm)
w: The centre's halal South Indian Muslim stall: fluffy, crisp-edged prata and banana-leaf meals with deeply spiced curries and tender mutton — on Honeycombers' 12 must-try list and named among the headline tenants by Time Out and Little Day Out.

dish: Warabimochi (matcha, hojicha, kinako), warabimochi milk drinks, kuromitsu-kinako soft serve
address: Waterway Point West Wing #01-72/73, 83 Punggol Central, Singapore 828761
w: The viral Kamakura warabimochi specialist (snaking queues at its 2024 Holland Village debut) opened its first dine-in café here in Oct 2024, with café-only warabimochi drinks, a kuromitsu soft serve dusted with kinako and a warabimochi-and-hot-matcha set — covered by Time Out, Mothership and Eatbook.
